decisions.reason: The affine-local-ring supplier explicitly assumes AC, whereas the original Definition asserted its identification without AC or an alternative proof. The contract incorrectly treated consuming that identification as choice-free. Added the inherited assumption and dependency, identified the reduced-chart supplier, and cited the affine-chart criterion through justified_by; the pointwise normality predicate and component-crossing argument are preserved.

The original Compatibility paragraph quantified over every principal open and claimed A_f had an integral closure inside k(X). At f=0, A_f is the zero ring and cannot embed unitally in the nonzero field k(X), so that claim is undefined; the cited supplier requires nonzero f. The repair gives the field identification only for nonzero f and treats the empty open by zero localized rings and conductor ideals, preserving full sheaf compatibility.

reviews.reason: Local author repair review checked the affine germ/localization argument under its actual AC hypothesis and its principal-open version for reduced charts. Normality is integral closedness of a domain at each stalk. Prime and maximal localization equivalence is supplied by the affine-chart criterion. In a reduced Noetherian chart, finite minimal-prime separation gives ab=0 and a/1,b/1 nonzero at a component crossing. Empty normality is vacuous. All 13 direct consumers already assume AC in their Statement/Definition or Facts/Given, so their exact uses remain sound.

Local author repair review checked the chartwise A subset B subset k(X) normalization interface, finite-generator denominator clearing for annihilator localization, nonzero principal opens and the f=0 zero-ring branch. Principal overlap refinements give the same conductor ideals in the shared normalized chart, so they glue. The finite quotient B/A vanishes locally exactly when B_m=A_m, equivalently when A_m is integrally closed; its support V(c) is the support of O_X/c. All three direct consumers use the unchanged conductor formula or quotient-support conclusion and remain sound.
